title: Dhubri
sub: From Assampedia, the free Assam encyclopedia
info: River port, Gurdwara Sri Tegh Bahadur Sahib
body:
Dhubri is a town at the western end of Assam, where the Brahmaputra is at its widest, near the borders with Bangladesh and West Bengal.

History

Dhubri was once an important river port and trading town. The Gurdwara Sri Tegh Bahadur Sahib here commemorates the visit of Guru Tegh Bahadur, and the town's Netai Dhubuni Ghat is linked in legend to the Behula–Lakhindar story.

Today

Dhubri district is largely agricultural, with jute, rice and fishing, and the town is a river and road link towards Cooch Behar and Bangladesh.
